messages:
anya: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a 'service fencing' approach to decouple session-manager + kv-cache from the runtime hotpath. intent: clearer RPC boundary, small shim adapter for compatibility, and an explicit 3-month tech-debt paydown cadence. looking for concerns, rollout risks, and ops requirements.

misha: sounds promising. can you sketch the surface area? which APIs change and what stays stable?

anya: good q. plan is to keep the public inference API identical. internal calls from runtime -> session-manager become an RPC (grpc/http) behind a thin compatibility shim. shim handles kv caching + prefix ops. no caller changes expected.

devon: major concern is latency tail — adding RPC could add ~0.8-2ms p50/p95 depending on host placement. do we have SLAs to absorb that? also need to think about co-location or in-process shim variants.

sam: unless we batch differently this could blow throughput for small seqs. any batching implications?

anya: batching will be preserved inside the session-manager side. the shim should support sync/async paths. co-locate option for Dedicated customers to avoid net hop. main win is ownership separation + safer deploys.

liz: operationally we need: traffic metrics per shim, contract checks, canary gates, and a kill-switch to revert to the old in-process path if perf regresses. also: plan for data migration of existing KV namespaces?

anya: yep — metrics + tracing is required. plan includes: (1) telemetry knobs (per-tenant histogram of rpc latency + error), (2) contract unit tests + fuzz for RPC surface, (3) canary by tenant and region, (4) feature flag to route selected traffic to shim. data migration: shim reads both stores (dual-read) for 4 weeks, then backfill / switch.

misha: dual-read is safe but doubles load. do we have capacity for that backfill window? need cost estimate.

devon: also add KV consistency expectations to the SLA doc. if shim can lag on deletes we must document eventual-consistency behavior.

sam: can we prototype a 'fast-path' shim that shortcuts when co-located (unix-socket) vs full rpc for cross-host? would lower tail.

anya: yep, prototype plan includes two modes: local-socket shim + grpc shim. we can auto-select based on topology.

liz: for rollout pulses: week 0 spike tests on staging, week 1 tiny tenant canary, week 2 broaden to 10% traffic, week 4 dual-read backfill, week 8 100% traffic + deprecate old path at week 12. adding paydown checkpoints at weeks 4/8/12 to close interfaces and remove hacks.

devon: +1 to checkpoints. we should also add a mandatory perf regression gate: any p95 > baseline + 15% blocks rollout.

anya: agreed. I'll add that to the RFC follow-up doc and include the perf gate.

infra-bot: created infra ticket INFRA-1347: "service-fence shim deploy + telemetry" (assign: devops).

misha: test plan notes: add contract tests to ci (grpc schema + golden kv snapshots), add chaos run where shim goes away mid-flight to validate rollback.

sam: FYI — embedding-heavy tenants might see cost delta from dual-read/backfill, flag them for owner review.

anya: noted. I'll produce a rough cost delta estimate before the canary kickoff.

liz: can we make a small checklist for on-call: how to detect shim regressions (alerts), how to flip kill-switch, and runbook steps for rollback?

anya: putting checklist in the follow-up doc. will ping infra + oncall channel once draft is ready.

devon: one last thought: long-term we should add an adapter registry so other services can opt into fencing pattern. avoids copy/paste of shims.

anya: good idea — add to backlog as "adapter-registry" epic; low-priority for this RFC but tracked.

misha: thanks — this feels pragmatic. happy to pair on the perf gating and contract tests.

anya: thanks all. I'll drop the follow-up doc link here once updated and schedule a 30min sync for Monday. :thumbsup:
